newsitem.title: HONG KONG: FOCUS-CITIC Pacific sells HK Telecom stake.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-CITIC Pacific sells HK Telecom stake.

text.p: CITIC Pacific Ltd ended months of speculation about a new China partner for Hongkong Telecom by announcing on Friday the sale of its 7.74 percent stake to China-controlled China Everbright Holdings Co Ltd.

The Hong Kong-based red chip conglomerate said it had agreed in principle on Thursday to sell its 904,686,181 shares for about HK$11.4 billion in cash to a wholly-owned subsidiary of China Everbright Holdings.
"It has been agreed in principle that the price will be calculated on the basis of HK$12.60 per Telecom share cum dividend," CITIC Pacific said in a statement.
"After the completion of the disposal, the company will have no further interests in Telecom shares," it added.
CITIC Pacific said the agreement had been reached on Thursday night but negotiations were still proceeding and no agreement had yet been signed.
"No agreement has yet been signed and there is no guarantee that the discussions will result in an agreement," it said.
Brian Smith, chairman of Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd and British-based Cable & Wireless group, which owns 58.5 percent of Hong Kong Telecom, welcomed the sale.

"We welcome the proposed investment by China Everbright in Hongkong Telecom. This substantial investment of Chinese State capital demonstrates continued confidence in Hongkong Telecom and Hong Kong through the 1997 transition and beyond," he said in a statement.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
China Everbright Holdings and CITIC Pacific's ultimate parent, China International Trust & Investment Corp, are both controlled by China's State Council.
China Everbright Holdings has three listed subsidiaries in Hong Kong -- China Everbright International Ltd, China Everbright Technology Ltd and China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd.

Zhu Xiaohua is the chairman of the holding company and its subsidiaries. He was a deputy governor of the People's Bank of China and the deputy director of the economics department at the Hong Kong branch of Xinhua news agency before joining the China Everbright group in July 1996.
Trading in shares of Hongkong Telecom and CITIC Pacific resumed on Friday afternoon after being suspended during the morning pending the announcement.
After furiously bidding up HongKong Telecom shares this week in anticipation of a deal, investors sold down the stock following the announcement.

HongKong Telecom shares were down HK$0.50 at HK$14.50 in afternoon trade, after jumping to a high of HK$15.90 immediately following the announcement. The stock had gained HK$1.80, or 13.6 percent, this week ahead of Friday's trading suspension.
CITIC Pacific shares rose HK$0.60 to HK$44.10 in Friday afternoon trade.
Shares in China Everbright International rose HK$0.15 to HK$1.71, China Everbright Technology gained HK$0.20 to HK$1.12 and China Everbright-IHD rose HK$0.45 to HK$8.55.
